The mission utilizes lightweight deployable solar panels to recharge rover batteries during its 100-day surface campaign.
key_points: MMX mission launched Oct 20, landing on Phobos in 2028
Idefix rover built by CNES/DLR powered by deployable solar panels
NASA JPL and Caltech involved in science payload and trajectory support
Microgravity sampling under intense radiation and thermal swings
connection_ideas: Flexible transparent polyimide substrates allow ultra-lightweight solar arrays crucial for planetary microgravity rovers.
Heliofold's Asian supply logistics enable swift delivery of specialized film samples for international planetary space missions.
Caltech and JPL researchers represent key target institutional partners for microgravity solar blanket testing.
Showcase how transparent PI blankets survive landing tumbles better than brittle rigid panel configurations.
R&D can investigate fine regolith dust adhesion on transparent polyimide versus traditional glass covercovers.
top_priorities.relevance_reason: Watchlist match for Caltech and JPL detailing solar power deployment on microgravity planetary exploration hardware.
